model_output.verdict: A dispatcher who moved up at Crossroads, with daily duties but little detail on the work handled.
write_up: You've moved from Dispatch Assistant to Dispatcher at Crossroads Regional Freight, after warehouse work at Hoosier Distribution. It's common for dispatch resumes to list daily duties this way, but yours won't stand out in a pile yet: a recruiter can't tell how many drivers or loads you handle, or what you do when a problem comes up.

Your line about tracking loads and updating customers is the strongest model: it names both the work and who gets the update. Your progression at Crossroads is easy to follow, too. The current role needs more detail to show what your dispatching work involves.
Let's start with the first Dispatcher line and add how many drivers you dispatch. Then work through the road issues, TMS tasks and driver-hours work using details you can stand behind.

cards.line: - Responsible for dispatching drivers
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows you dispatch drivers, but not how many or what you coordinate for them. That's central to the job you're presenting.
cards.example: Responsible for dispatching [number] drivers and coordinating [dispatch work]
cards.question: How many drivers do you dispatch, and what do you coordinate for them?

cards.line: - Track loads and update customers on delivery status
cards.cannot_tell: This names two useful parts of the job. It doesn't show how many loads you track or how often you update customers.
cards.example: Track [number] loads [time period] and update customers on delivery status [update frequency]
cards.question: How many loads do you track, and how often do you update customers?

cards.line: - Handle driver issues on the road
cards.cannot_tell: Driver issues could cover a lot. A recruiter can't tell what comes up or what you do to handle it.
cards.example: Handle [types of driver issues] on the road by [what you do]
cards.question: What kinds of issues do drivers bring you, and what do you do when they come up?

cards.line: - Use TMS software daily
cards.cannot_tell: McLeod TMS is already in your skills. What isn't clear is what you use the software to do during a dispatch day.
cards.question: What dispatch tasks do you carry out in the TMS?

cards.line: - Work with the safety team on driver hours
cards.cannot_tell: Working with the safety team could mean several things. Your part in managing driver hours isn't clear yet.
cards.example: Work with the safety team on driver hours by [your part in the work]
cards.question: What do you do with the safety team when you're working on driver hours?

cards.line: - Helped dispatchers with paperwork
cards.cannot_tell: This leaves the paperwork and your part in it open to guesswork. Naming both would show what you learned in the assistant role.
cards.question: What paperwork did you help with, and what did you do with it?

fit.note: Your experience points toward dispatch work in regional trucking, with a move from assistant to dispatcher at the same company. The resume needs more detail on the drivers and loads you handle to show the breadth of that work.
